text:
Rory McIlroy does not think the Memorial Tournament milkshakes are anything special.(Image: Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto)

The Memorial Tournament might be a storied competition helmed by Jack Nicklaus with a massive $20 million prize pool, but for many golfers, the renowned milkshakes steal the show — though Rory McIlroy isn't among them.

Nicklaus, a titan of the sport, established the Memorial Tournament at Muirfield Village Golf Club back in 1976.

The legend aimed to deliver top-tier golf to his cherished Ohio, and boldly suggested the event could rival even the Masters, a major championship he captured six times. McIlroy has made his return following another brief hiatus from competition. It comes after Rory McIlroy named two events on his career bucket list after his second Masters win.

A post-round milkshake might have helped settle Scheffler's nerves after the initial round, though McIlroy remains puzzled by all the fanfare.

Players, spouses, caddies and relatives can grab 16-ounce milkshakes at Muirfield, with reports suggesting up to 600 have been dished out in a single day. Each shake packs a whopping 1,200 calories, with the Buckeye flavor reigning as the crowd favorite.

With 14 flavors available and customization options, most golfers rave about the shakes, some even indulging in several per day. McIlroy, however, isn't joining the chorus of praise.

Jordan Spieth walks to the driving range with a milkshake in hand last year.(Image: 2025 Ben Jared/PGA TOUR)

Speaking to GolfWeek back in 2022, McIlroy remarked, "I guess I don't want to get in trouble here, but like I – like the milkshakes are good. I've had milkshakes that are just as good elsewhere.

"Maybe because it's Muirfield Village, they taste better, I don't know. I'm happy with having one or two a week. I'm certainly not one of the guys that's standing there getting two a day."

Rich milkshakes have become a tradition for players, families, and media members at the Memorial Tournament.(Image: 2023 Chris Condon/PGA TOUR)

Former Ryder Cup captain Keegan Bradley has a different take, suggesting the milkshakes are among the top attractions at the Memorial Tournament. "The milkshakes are the really good thing about Memorial," Bradley mentioned on the Games With Names podcast.

"... I think [Nicklaus] makes his own ice cream. Like, they do everything to the max."

Each shake is freshly prepared to order and delivered within three minutes. While the creamy treats may be Muirfield's signature offering, distinct from the iconic pimento cheese and egg salad sandwiches at Augusta National, Nicklaus is confident his event stands among the elite.

"I think in many ways, we're better than the Masters," Nicklaus said. "But then again the Masters is pretty sensational. But we've done pretty well here. And I think the people in central Ohio have embraced it."

Nicklaus also maintains a cherished tradition at Muirfield, greeting the winner with a handshake moments after they complete the 18th hole.

"The players love it because I'm sort of trying to take this tournament a little bit of the image of how I would like to be treated as a player,"

Nicklaus explained. "I would like to walk out onto a golf course that's in good condition. I like to walk out to a golf course that's challenging and pretty. I'd like to be embraced by the fans and get taken care of in the clubhouse.

"And I think that's what's made the golf tournament. You know, I've played in a few golf tournaments, so I think that probably made it a little bit better over time."

Meanwhile, McIlroy showed class in a heartwarming interaction with a young fan at a tournament.
